## Grammar

Basic word order is VSO; it has prepositions. In the noun phrase: possessed before the possessor; noun before the adjective; noun before the demonstrative; noun before the numeral; noun before the relative clause. Overall it is head-initial.
It has a definite article after the noun, no indefinite article, no case marking on nouns, no alignment marking (subject and object are not told apart by form), singular and plural, no gender or noun classes.
Verbs mark future; there are no evidentials. Negation uses a negator before the verb; yes/no questions use intonation alone. Verbs do not agree with their arguments.
Other features: an inclusive/exclusive 'we' distinction; serial verbs; verb reduplication; a copula; a bound causative; a bound passive; question words left in place; a decimal counting base.
